title: Increasing-tuple module-sheaf terms are products of open direct images
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X.\mathrm{Opens}$ any finite family and $G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module. Let $C$ be the explicit complex [def-pc-s3-alternating-cech-sheaf-construction], with intersections $W_t$. For every $k\in\mathbb N$ there is an isomorphism $C^k\cong\prod_{t:\operatorname{Fin}(k+1)\hookrightarrow_o\operatorname{Fin}(r)}(W_t\hookrightarrow X)_*(G|_{W_t})$. No cover, affineness or quasi-coherence is assumed; empty products are included.

proof.text: The canonical product-intersection isomorphism W times V isomorphic to V intersect W gives an O(V)-linear presheaf isomorphism between P_W and the underlying presheaf of the over-site extension of G.over W. Its component maps are restrictions along that isomorphism and are natural in V. Apply module sheafification and the counit isomorphism on the extension sheaf. The over-site equivalence identifies restriction with restriction to W.toScheme; uniqueness of right adjoints identifies the extension sheaf with j_* of G restricted to W. Module sheafification is additive, hence preserves finite biproducts and finite products. Compose its finite-product comparison with the product of the preceding component isomorphisms in degree k. Empty tuple types give the same empty-product comparison. The Lean proof uses the Mathlib APIs overPushforwardOverAdj, overFunctorEquiv, Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq, sheafificationAdjunction and PreservesProduct.iso.
